messages:
maria: heads up — ran a quick FP8 vs INT8 prefetch KV sweep on canary, short summary below. FP8 saves ~30% memory but p99 tails worsened on long-context traces. wondering if it's alignment/eviction related :thinking_face:

samir: can you drop the raw numbers and command?

maria: sure — here's the exact run I did: ```./tools/kv_bench --model=ivy30b --quant=fp8 --kv-mode=prefetch --batch=4 --seq=2048 --prefill_stride=128 --runs=100``` results: p50=3.2ms p95=12.3ms p99=78.1ms mem=6.8GB cpu=%util 42

maria: then swapped --quant=int8 (same flags) => p50=3.4ms p95=11.9ms p99=62.4ms mem=9.5GB cpu=%util 58

chao: interesting — fp8 wins mem but loses p99. two quick hypotheses: 1) fp8 dequant path + KV prefetch interleaving causes extra dequant stalls on cache-miss chains, 2) block alignment/stride causing partial loads and extra memcpy.

chao: did you try smaller prefill_stride? we've seen stride=64 reduce tail in similar runs.

maria: not yet. re-ran with --prefill_stride=64: fp8 p99 dropped to 55.2ms (mem 6.9GB). so alignment definitely helped.

samir: aha. does INT8 improve with stride=64 too?

maria: int8 at stride=64: p99=48.9ms mem=9.6GB. still lower p99 than fp8 but memory delta persists.

liz: could this be a KV eviction thrash when prefetch + fp8 reduce memory and increase fill rate? we need allocation/evict counters. can we capture `kv_metrics.evictions/sec` and `prefetch.misses`?

maria: added counters in that next run. fp8 (stride=64) => evictions/sec=12.4 prefetch.misses=3.1. int8 => evictions/sec=6.8 prefetch.misses=2.7

chao: that supports eviction thrash theory. fp8 packs more entries so eviction frequency goes up; prefetch then triggers dequant stalls as it chases evicted entries -> tail spikes.

samir: operational question — if we push FP8 to prod for cost savings we might regress latency for long-doc workflows. we need a rollout policy: prefer fp8 for short-context routes, fallback to int8 for large seq.

maria: agreed. quick A/B on canary traffic (10%) with route-based policy seems fine. also testing hybrid: fp8 for kv storage + int8 dequant on hot paths? not trivial.

kv-benchmark-bot: summary artifact uploaded: https://artifacts.internal/kv_runs/1735555555-summary.csv 

kv-benchmark-bot: snippet: ```quant,seq,p50,p95,p99,mem
fp8,512,1.8,6.2,32.0,4.1GB
fp8,2048,3.2,12.3,78.1,6.8GB
fp8_s64,2048,3.1,11.8,55.2,6.9GB
int8,2048,3.4,11.9,62.4,9.5GB
int8_s64,2048,3.3,11.5,48.9,9.6GB
```

liz: nice. can we add a tiny cost calc line? memory reduction -> fewer GPUs per shard. approximate: fp8 sharding factor +1.4x density -> ~28% cheaper infra for these routes. add to doc.

maria: will add cost delta and a proposed rollout: 1) shadow traffic run for 24h, 2) 10% canary route for short-context routes, 3) monitor p99 + evictions, auto-roll back on >10% p99 regression.

chao: also recommend trying AWQ/GPTQ variants — AWQ's blocking layout might avoid the partial-load penalty we saw. run AWQ-prefetch w/ stride=64 and compare.
extra_notes: thread focuses on KV cache quantization prefetch experiments comparing FP8 and INT8. messages include commands, micro-results, metrics, hypothesis, and rollout plan. contains bot artifact link and small CSV snippet. all messages are short/slack-like.
